clips.hook: He turned down a quarter million at 23
clips.title: He turned down a quarter million at 23. Then AI built his idea in 24 hours
clips.caption: At 23, Zain turned down £250,000 in investor cash because he was working on the wrong thing. Later he rambled his idea at an AI app and it popped up on screen.

lower.title: Zain, co-founder of Saath
lower.sub: Turned down a quarter million in funding

clips.hook: Their university tried to stop them. Now it wants in.
clips.title: 3 students hit €130K ARR in month one. Their university tried to stop them
clips.caption: Isabel, Andreas and Eric hit €130,000 ARR in Klar's first month, all from word of mouth. The university that tried to stop them now wants to work with them.
clips.end: Would you drop out of college for this?

clips.hook: Why your favourite local restaurant closes
clips.title: Big chains win on software. He built it for small restaurants
clips.caption: Every year 30% of new local restaurants close, while big chains spend millions on software. Jaleel built QuickTables to give small restaurants the same tools.

lower.title: Jaleel, QuickTables co-founder
lower.sub: 30% of new restaurants close every year

clips.end: What problem do your local shops have?

clips.hook: A candle for his dad became €1.3M for charity
clips.title: A candle for his dad turned into €1.3 million for nonprofits
clips.caption: Before every hospital checkup, Quinten told his dad he was lighting a candle for him. That became WeGlow: more than 35,000 candles lit and more than €1.3 million raised.
clips.end: Who would you light a candle for?

clips.hook: His engineers resisted. 16,000 users in 3 months
clips.title: His engineers resisted the new tool. 16,000 users in 3 months
clips.caption: Lex Deak's engineers met Lovable with reluctance and fear. He gave them time to explore it, and about three months after launch WNTD has 15,000 to 16,000 users.
clips.end: Was your team scared of AI at first?

clips.hook: His wife's flight got cancelled on Valentine's Day
clips.title: A cancelled Valentine's Day flight showed him what's broken in travel
clips.caption: On Valentine's Day, Nico's wife was stuck in a snowstorm 500 miles away and her flight got cancelled. Hundreds of travel apps, and none of them helped.

lower.title: Nico Wittenberg, AVARA founder
lower.sub: His wife was stuck 500 miles away

clips.end: Has a booking app ever saved your trip?

clips.title: College hasn't changed since 1088. Their AI tutor learns how you learn
clips.caption: The first university opened in Bologna in 1088 and the system hasn't changed. 40% of students drop out, and Klar's founders say learning has to adapt to every person.

lower.title: Isabel, Andreas and Eric, Klar
lower.sub: 40% of students drop out of their degree

clips.hook: One AI that teaches you the way you learn
clips.title: One AI tutor for flashcards, videos and quizzes
clips.caption: Flashcards, videos, images, summaries, quizzes: Klar does all of it and always knows where you're at. Thousands of students were waiting to learn differently.
clips.end: Flashcards or video: how do you study?

clips.hook: He was told he'd need $500K. He used AI instead.
clips.title: He was told he'd need $500K to build it. He used AI instead
clips.caption: Jaleel was told he'd need about $500,000 to build his restaurant software. Instead he built QuickTables with Lovable, so restaurants can focus on food and leave marketing to them.

clips.title: 90% of restaurant owners don't want a ghost kitchen
clips.caption: 90% of restaurant owners don't want to run a ghost kitchen. QuickTables gives customers points and discounts for picking up their food instead.

lower.title: QuickTables founding team
lower.sub: 90% of owners don't want ghost kitchens

clips.end: Would points get you to pick up food?

clips.caption: Zain cheers for England but eats biryani at home. With his best friend Habib he built Saath, a community-led fund for locally-led projects across South Asia.
